clue.text: Missing substance found by female in casuals

indicators.note: the female letter is placed inside the pair of casual words, between them

parts.note: airy means casual or offhand, and the plural asks for two of them

explanation.surface: Something lacking was discovered by a woman among the casual wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casuals' is not clothing: it is two lots of AIRY (offhand), with F between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas called airy-fairy are vague and impractical, lacking any real substance.

clue.text: Third in slalom will help procure Olympic bronze, perhaps

indicators.note: the third letter in each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Finishing third in the downhill race would win an Olympic bronze medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronze is a mixture of copper and tin, an example of a blended metal.

clue.text: Sorry fellow hiding key one retrieves

indicators.note: the key is concealed inside the sorry fellow

parts.note: a ruer is one who rues, a sorry person
ESC is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A remorseful man conceals a key that someone else finds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who saves or recovers another from danger is one who retrieves them.

clue.text: A horse gypsies reared under substantial illusion

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means placed after

parts.note: fat means substantial or large

indicators.note: rose up, which in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a nag is a horse
the Roma are a Romani people

explanation.surface: A horse that travellers raised was a hefty mirage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reared' means rose up, so in this down clue the horse and the gypsies are read from the bottom upwards; 'under' places them below the substantial word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a kind of mirage seen over the sea, so it is an optical illusion.

clue.text: Would that one move quickly, clutching leg?

parts.note: I is one as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: the fast-moving word grips the leg inside it

parts.note: to fly is to move quickly
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: Wishing someone could run fast while holding an injured limb.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a wish for something that is not so: if only it were true.

clue.text: Especially universal, my item's most appealing to consumers

indicators.note: read as specially made, so the letters are specially arranged

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A product pitched as universally attractive to buyers.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is yummiest tastes best, so it most pleases those who eat it.

clue.text: Prison system that's good acceptable to socially-superior convict

parts.note: U means upper-class, acceptable to the socially superior, as in U and non-U usage
an old lag is a long-serving convict

explanation.surface: A prison network deemed fine by snobbish types for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet network of forced-labour camps was known by this acronym-based name.

clue.text: Creature in retreat from Kew?

indicators.note: the retreat is taken away from Kew's word

parts.note: Kew is famous for its botanic garden in west London
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: An animal hiding out somewhere near the botanic gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London; GARDEN without DEN leaves GAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The gar is a long-snouted fish, a living creature.

clue.text: Paper for ladies and old men placed in lounge

indicators.note: the old men are put inside the lounge word

parts.note: to loll is to lounge
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Newspapers for the women and pensioners set out in the sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' is the verb loll, not a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet tissue comes on this cardboard tube, and the ladies is a lavatory.

clue.text: Dull American clothes heartless nursemaid put on elderly relative

indicators.note: dresses, so it wraps itself around the other pieces

parts.note: gray is the American spelling of grey, dull

indicators.note: the whole middle of nursemaid is removed, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: to add is to put on

explanation.surface: A drab US garment worn by a callous nanny over an old relation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb. GRAY dresses ND (nursemaid without its heart) plus ADD.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an American informal word for a grandfather, an elderly family member.

clue.text: Those old, endless rambles in the country

indicators.note: to ramble is to wander about, so the letters wander into a new order
the last letter of the word old is cut off

explanation.surface: Elderly folk out walking somewhere in a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims OLD to OL; THOSE plus OL is then rearranged by 'rambles'.
explanation.definitionFit: This landlocked kingdom is entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Having a very fine memory, recalled dancer

indicators.note: called back, so the whole string is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: OK means fine or all right
RAM is computer memory

explanation.surface: Someone with a superb memory remembered a ballet performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns AVOKRAM round as one string. Alicia Markova was a celebrated English ballerina.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Alicia Markova was a famous British prima ballerina of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Reader recited letter adjacent to Guardian leader

indicators.note: spoken out, so we want the word that sounds like the letter

parts.note: in the word Guardian the letter next to the leading G is U

explanation.surface: Someone read out a letter beside a newspaper's editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian leader' tempts as an editorial; it is the G at the head of the word Guardian, and its neighbour is U.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer addresses the person reading with this pronoun, so the reader is the one being spoken to.

clue.text: Very little time to get factory back — one needs to be seized

indicators.note: the numeral is grabbed and held inside the other pieces

parts.note: a mill is a factory
to back a motion is to second it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rush to buy back a works before someone gets arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousandth of a second is a tiny interval of time.

clue.text: Old master criticised about book gets aggravated

parts.note: ex means former
an ace is an expert, a master

indicators.note: the criticism word goes around the book

parts.note: to rate someone is to scold them

explanation.surface: A painter of old works, slammed over a volume, gets irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old master' tempts as a painter; it is EX plus ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exacerbate a problem is to make it worse, so it is aggravated.

clue.text: City, missing final, had not done well

indicators.note: the word had loses its last letter

parts.note: rare meat is undercooked, the opposite of well done

explanation.surface: A team missed out on the final and played badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing final' looks like sport, but it trims HAD to HA.
explanation.definitionFit: Harare is the capital city of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Cause of bitterness put an end to game

parts.note: hops give beer its bitter taste
to scotch a rumour is to put an end to it

explanation.surface: Something that causes resentment ended the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitterness' is the taste of bitter beer, not resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Children hop through numbered squares chalked on the ground in this playground game.

clue.text: Went for turkey, and was ill

parts.note: turkey is slang for a fool, as is ass
ailed means was unwell

explanation.surface: Someone chose the turkey dish and was then sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turkey' suggests Christmas dinner; here it is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To be assailed is to be attacked, and to go for someone is to attack them.

clue.text: Where to find my North Carolina chaff?

definitions.text: Where to find my North Carolina chaff?

parts.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise
to chaff is to tease, as is to rib

explanation.surface: Asking where the husks of a North Carolina harvest are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaff' is the verb to tease. Read whole, the clue asks where Carolina grain is stored.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncrib is a ventilated store for maize, where its husks would be found.

clue.text: Spotted US President at drinks party

parts.note: James K Polk was the eleventh US President

indicators.note: to drink something in is to take it inside, so at swallows the party

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: An American leader seen at a cocktail party.
explanation.definitionFit: A polka-dot pattern is made of spots, so fabric with it is spotted.

clue.text: After lake crossing now, finally, taking off wader

indicators.note: the rest follows the lake letter
the letter cuts across the middle of the mimicry word

parts.note: taking someone off is mimicking them, aping

indicators.note: the last letter of now is taken

explanation.surface: A bird finally flies off after crossing a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' suggests flight; it means mimicking, APING.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing, or peewit, is a plover found on wetlands, a wading bird.

clue.text: Privileged class score with dope

parts.note: gen and dope are both slang for inside information
a try is a score in rugby

explanation.surface: The elite settle a debt with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs, but it is information (GEN). A try is a scoring touchdown in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the well-born landed class just below the nobility.

clue.text: What to do to hide deceit short of meditating?

parts.note: tanning is the process applied to an animal hide

indicators.note: the deceit word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a trick is a deceit

explanation.surface: Wondering how to conceal a con that stops short of thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a verb (conceal), but it is an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantric practice uses ritual meditation, so it relates to that discipline.

clue.text: Bubbly-sounding partners love treatment

indicators.note: said out loud, so we want letters that sound like the bubbly word

parts.note: fizzy means bubbly
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A lively couple share their affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partners' is just a link: the pieces go together.
explanation.definitionFit: Physio is short for physiotherapy, a remedial treatment for injury.

clue.text: Vengeful seaman at a pinch — a furious sailor

indicators.note: wild with rage, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a rank of sailor

explanation.surface: A raging mariner, if it came to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Melville's captain in Moby-Dick is driven by his thirst for revenge on the white whale.

clue.text: Drink pop and have a bite

definitions.meaning: a small measure of spirits, a tot
to go somewhere briefly, as in pop out to the shops
to give a small sharp bite or pinch

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a tot of spirits, a quick dash somewhere, and a small sharp bite.

clue.text: Weigh up lesser problems, to an extent

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom
only part of the words is used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Consider minor issues to some degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to an extent' takes SSERP from lesSER Problems; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh on someone is to press heavily on them.

clue.text: Scaffolder arriving on time is prompt

indicators.note: the scaffolder comes after, landing on the time letter

parts.note: a rigger erects scaffolding

explanation.surface: A builder turning up punctually is prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prompt' looks like an adjective (punctual) but is the verb: to prompt is to set off.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to prompt or set it off.

clue.text: Big blow having point deducted for miss

indicators.note: the point is subtracted from the big blow

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A heavy punch loses a point for a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big blow' sounds like a punch; it is a strong wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Gal is an informal word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Deliver without the box

definitions.meaning: to deliver is to liberate or release
the box is slang for the TV set, so with none of it you are free of a set

explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone is to release them, and a home with no TV set is set-free.

clue.text: Say, what about Liberal philosopher!

indicators.note: turned about, so the two short pieces are read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
eh is an exclamation like what

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a party member's ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns EGEH round to HEGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegel was the German idealist thinker behind the dialectic.

clue.text: American sticks having cut in benefits

indicators.note: the cut is placed inside the benefits

parts.note: boons are blessings or benefits
to dock is to cut, as with a tail or wages

explanation.surface: Someone reliant on welfare suffers a reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticks' is the noun for remote countryside, as in living out in the sticks, not pieces of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Boondocks is American slang for remote backwoods, the equivalent of the sticks.
